summary.oneLiner: Nykaa delivered record revenue and profitability growth in FY26, with EBITDA margin expanding to 7.5% and PAT margin hitting 2%, driven by accelerated growth in House of Nykaa brands and profitable turnaround in Fashion; the company is now a dominant omnichannel platform in beauty and fashion with AI-enhanced customer acquisition and brand partnerships like Nike and H&M creating new revenue streams.
summary.business: FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa) sells and distributes beauty, fashion and wellness products to Indian consumers through its own online platforms and apps and through an owned physical retail network, complemented by a B2B distribution arm and a portfolio of owned consumer brands. The platform curates global, homegrown and emerging brands and pairs them with content-led discovery, expert guidance and in-store experiences, serving tech-savvy consumers with a particular focus on Gen Z and millennials. Alongside the marketplace and inventory-led retail business, House of Nykaa builds and scales the company's own beauty and fashion brands, while Superstore by Nykaa supplies the unorganised beauty retail trade.

Beauty: Nykaa online beauty platform and app
Nykaa beauty stores (313 stores across 99 cities)
Nykaa Luxe stores (15 new premium stores in FY2026)
Dedicated Perfumery stores for luxury fragrances
4,400+ beauty and personal care brands, including Chanel Beauty & Fragrance, Armani Beauty, Maison Margiela Fragrances, Kylie Cosmetics, SK-II, Paula's Choice, La Roche-Posay, Anua and IT Cosmetics
Fashion: ~5,700 fashion brands across lifestyle categories, including partnerships with Nike and H&M
B2B: Superstore by Nykaa (serving nearly 5,00,000 onboarded retailers across 1,200 cities)

currentContext.strengths: Largest specialty beauty retail store network in India - 313 beauty stores across 99 cities, with a record 76 new stores added in FY2026|Preferred gateway for global beauty brands entering India - L'Oreal, Estee Lauder, Shiseido, Puig and Amorepacific partner with Nykaa, and 200+ international beauty brands were added in FY2026 including exclusive launches|Assortment breadth and curation - 10,000+ global and domestic brands on the platform, 4,400+ beauty and personal care brands and ~5,700 fashion brands as on March 31, 2026|Cumulative customer base of more than 55 million (45 million beauty, 11 million fashion), described as India's largest and most valuable beauty customer base|Owned-brand building capability - House of Nykaa combines consumer insight, in-house R&D, packaging expertise and 360-degree marketing, with brands sold across Nykaa, stores, brand-owned channels, general trade, marketplaces and exports|B2B reach into the unorganised beauty retail market - Superstore by Nykaa serves nearly 5,00,000 onboarded retailers across 1,200 cities|Premium customer mix - Nykaa Fashion's Average Order Value of Rs 4,600 is around 60% higher than comparable platforms, and Nykaa customers spend roughly 5x the India average|Fulfilment density supporting service levels - 70% of beauty orders across the top 110 cities are delivered within 24-36 hours
currentContext.strategies: Deliver profitable growth with efficient capital utilisation and strong unit economics, with capital allocation anchored in Return on Capital Employed.|Maintain balance-sheet and working-capital discipline - shorten the operating cycle through faster inventory turnover and continue reducing net debt.|Run a content-first omnichannel ecosystem that integrates content, commerce and convenience so customers can discover, learn and shop across digital platforms and physical stores.|Curate a differentiated assortment of global, homegrown and owned brands using consumer insights, market intelligence and trend forecasting, refreshed through innovative products, exclusive launches and emerging categories.|Embed Generative AI and analytics across customer service and customer experience - AI-powered self-service, voice bots for order queries, personalised recommendations and virtual consultations.|Deepen collaborative planning with brand partners through the CPFR framework and an integrated S&OP process with AI-powered demand sensing, supported by an Auto Replenishment System that manages lead times and demand variability.|Automate and digitise operations - EDI-based partner integration, a digitised end-to-end order lifecycle, faster order processing, better fill rates and improved inventory freshness.|Build sustainable and responsible partnerships - responsible sourcing, expanded use of recyclable and eco-friendly packaging, reduction of single-use plastics through supplier collaboration, localised fulfilment and MSME support.|Rationalise the legal-entity structure to consolidate businesses and remove duplication - the online B2B beauty business was demerged from FSN Distribution into Nykaa E-Retail and Iluminar Media was amalgamated into Nykaa Fashion, both operationalised with effect from May 29, 2025.|Increase ownership of owned-brand subsidiaries - stake in Dot & Key Wellness raised to 90.06%, Earth Rhythm to ~75.83%, and the remaining 40% of Nudge Wellness acquired to make it a wholly-owned subsidiary.|Improve financial transparency for shareholders through granular segment-level disclosure for Beauty and Fashion and sustained investor engagement (quarterly earnings calls, quarterly revenue updates, an annual Investor Day, store and Nykaaland visits).|The Company has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations setting out the internal and external factors the Board considers in determining pay-out. For FY2025-26 the Board did not recommend any dividend on equity shares and decided to retain the entire profit for the year in the statement of profit and loss, i.e. the stance remains full reinvestment. Management describes its capital allocation strategy as "firmly anchored in Return on Capital Employed", combining balance-sheet discipline (working capital efficiency and net debt reduction) with a commitment to generate higher operating cash flow through efficient working capital management and optimised capital expenditure. Forward intent is to keep investing in the core growth engines while taking a phased approach to new, emerging opportunity areas through either organic initiatives or strategic inorganic acquisitions. The Company reports a long-term credit rating of CRISIL A - Stable. As on March 31, 2026 the Company has no associate or joint venture; it has eleven direct subsidiaries and ten step-down subsidiaries.|BRSR disclosures carry Reasonable Assurance in line with ISAE 3000 (Revised) from TUV India Pvt. Ltd., covering FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited and its subsidiary Nykaa E-Retail Limited.|100% of R&D investment in both FY2025-26 and FY2024-25 was directed at improving own-brand product formulations by incorporating non-hazardous and environmentally friendly ingredients.|0.29% of capital expenditure in FY2025-26 (0.24% in FY2024-25) was spent on upgrading infrastructure at offices and warehouses with energy-efficient technologies to reduce electricity consumption and lower carbon emissions.|The Company has formally adopted a Sustainable Sourcing Policy and states it has procedures in place for sustainable sourcing.|Progressive incorporation of renewable energy across facilities alongside continuing improvement in operational and energy efficiency (stated as the mitigation for the climate-change material issue; no dated target or renewable-share percentage is disclosed).|Packaging and waste commitments with value-chain partners: expand the use of recyclable and eco-friendly packaging, reduce single-use plastics through supplier collaboration, and enable localised fulfilment to lower environmental impact.|Supplier inclusion: 8,700+ MSME partners, with MSMEs engaged for packaging procurement and supported in building a resilient supply ecosystem.|Human rights expectations are reinforced across suppliers and partners through contractual provisions; awareness programmes for selected value chain partners cover fire safety, emergency response, road safety and POSH guidelines.|Governance and ethics: an Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bribery Policy applying to Directors, Officers, Employees, subsidiaries, affiliates, contractors and suppliers; annual Code of Conduct and POSH training; a whistle-blower Speak-up helpline run by an external agency with direct access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee. Nil fines/penalties and no bribery/corruption disciplinary actions in FY2025-26.|Information security: the Company's processes and controls are ISO 27001 certified, supported by periodic internal and external technology assessments.|Diversity: women are 27.27% of the Board of Directors (3 of 11) and 40% of Key Management Personnel (2 of 5); women are 48.20% of total employees.|Customer grievance performance: 100% of customer complaints resolved in FY2026, with no complaints pending resolution at year-end across any stakeholder group.
currentContext.expansion: Nykaa's expansion in FY2026 was footprint- and network-led rather than plant-led. The beauty retail network was expanded by a record 76 new stores during the year, and the premium format was scaled with 15 new Nykaa Luxe stores plus dedicated Perfumery stores for luxury fragrances; Nykaa Now was rolled out to enable rapid delivery. On fulfilment, the CFO's message describes a network of 44 warehouses across 15 cities that "significantly strengthened our delivery capabilities and customer experience", with the result that 70% of beauty orders across the top 110 cities are now delivered within 24-36 hours. Assortment expansion accompanied the physical build-out: 200+ new international beauty brands were launched in FY2026, and Nykaa Fashion added 1,250+ brands during the year (680+ in women's fashion, 280+ in home and accessories, 170+ in men's fashion and 120+ in kids' wear). The CFO states that capital expenditure during FY2026 "was deployed exclusively towards high-velocity physical store expansion (76 additions) and strengthening our technology infrastructure". Within total capex, the BRSR reports that 0.29% in FY2025-26 (0.24% in FY2024-25) went to upgrading infrastructure at offices and warehouses with energy-efficient technologies. Looking forward, management says it will continue to expand the physical retail store footprint, make deliberate investments to acquire new customers and improve order-to-delivery speeds, leverage technology and automation for efficiency, optimise capital expenditure, and take a phased approach to investing in new, emerging opportunity areas through either organic initiatives or strategic inorganic acquisitions. No commissioning timelines, project names or rupee project budgets are disclosed in the routed text.
currentContext.mdna: Asset productivity is being lifted by lower warehouse and store intensity relative to turnover and by the rising salience of asset-light businesses such as Fashion and House of Nykaa.|Management attributes margin expansion to operating leverage - "operational excellence coupled with scale efficiencies".|Working capital efficiency improved sharply, with the operating cycle reducing to 28 days from 34 days in FY2025 aided by faster inventory turnover; inventory days were lower by 4 days while receivables improved by 2 days.|The return profile is being driven by balance-sheet discipline, with net debt nearly halving during the year.|Demand engagement metrics are the stated growth drivers - monthly average unique visitors, annual unique transacting customers and orders all grew, supported by content-led discovery and a curated assortment.|Trust, authenticity, quality assurance and personalised, expert-assisted experiences are cited as the basis for repeat engagement and customer loyalty.

risks.risk: Product quality and safety across a third-party supply base
risks.note: The business model depends on third-party suppliers and partner manufacturers, so ingredients, formulations and finished products need rigorous oversight; any lapse could lead to regulatory scrutiny and weaken customer confidence in products offered on the platform. Mitigated through responsible supplier selection, manufacturing aligned with Good Manufacturing Practices, consumer testing and post-development validation.

As an e-commerce platform handling sensitive customer data, any unauthorised access, misuse or fraud could lead to financial implications, regulatory scrutiny and a decline in customer confidence. This is the only material issue the BRSR classifies as a pure Risk with negative financial implications only. Mitigated through advanced cybersecurity controls, periodic internal and external technology assessments, ISO 27001 certified processes and controls, monitoring of high-risk activity and review of seller transaction histories.

risks.risk: Talent attraction and retention in a high-attrition market
risks.note: Nykaa operates in a dynamic talent market characterised by high attrition and intense competition for skilled professionals. The BRSR reports permanent-employee turnover of 32% in FY2025-26 (30% in FY2024-25), with female turnover at 40%. Mitigated through learning and development, engagement initiatives, employer branding and induction of experienced professionals into critical leadership roles.

risks.risk: Responsible supply chain exposed to geopolitical, climate and infrastructure shocks
risks.note: The value chain remains sensitive to geopolitical developments, climate-related events, infrastructure limitations and rising sustainability expectations, each of which can influence operating performance, customer experience and brand perception. Mitigated through a decentralised, locally anchored supply chain, MSME engagement for packaging procurement and contractual human-rights expectations for suppliers and partners.

risks.risk: Responsible marketing, service delivery and consumer-protection compliance
risks.note: Customer-related risk can emerge from breakdowns in service delivery, non-compliant or inaccurate promotional messaging, and evolving legal obligations including ASCI norms and consumer protection requirements. Mitigated through an integrated multi-channel marketing approach that reduces dependence on any one medium, labelling compliance, and structured grievance and satisfaction tracking.

risks.risk: Climate change, GHG emissions and energy-efficiency regulation
risks.note: Climate-related disruptions including extreme weather events may affect operational continuity, while compliance with evolving emissions regulations could place additional pressure on operating costs. The Company says it is progressively incorporating renewable energy across facilities while enhancing operational and energy efficiency.

risks.risk: Packaging and waste management under evolving regulation
risks.note: Listed as a material risk-and-opportunity in the BRSR material-issues table in light of evolving regulation; the rationale text is cut off in the routed extract, so only the identification of the issue is supported.

Structural concentration disclosed rather than labelled as a risk: retail sale via e-commerce accounts for 95% of the listed entity's turnover, markets served are Pan India with International shown as Not Applicable (exports sit in a separate subsidiary, FSN International), and 100% of loans and advances and 100% of investments are with related parties. Customer grievances filed were 5,879 in FY2025-26 (6,933 in FY2024-25), all resolved with none pending.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
